t: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Army Reserve on active duty under sections 10211, 10302, and 3038 of title 10, United States Code, or while serving on active duty under section 12301(d) of title 10, United States Code, in connection with performing duty specified in section 12310(a) of title 10, United States Code, or while undergoing reserve training, or while performing drills or equivalent duty or other duty, and expenses authorized by section 16131 of title 10, United States Code; and for payments to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund, $3,043,170,000.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision funding pay and related expenses for Army Reserve personnel and payments to the Military Retirement Fund. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation language here; the provision simply designates money for specified purposes.
fable.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Army Reserve on active duty

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes funding for the pay and expenses of Army Reserve personnel and payments to a military retirement fund. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are federal employees and federal funds.
qwen_block.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Army Reserve on active duty... and for payments to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund, $3,043,170,000.

opus.w: This provision only sets aside money for Army Reserve pay, allowances, and related costs, plus payments to the Military Retirement Fund. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The statutory cross-references and duty-related words describe personnel categories, not a way for outside parties to take part in decisions.
opus.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Army Reserve

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations for the pay and expenses of Army Reserve personnel and payments to the military retirement fund. Army Reserve personnel are federal employees/military members, which places them inside the federal government according to the definition. There is no consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities).
qwen_chat.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Army Reserve on active duty... and for payments to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "personnel of the Army Reserve" are outside the federal government because they are reservists. However, the definition explicitly states that "federal employees" are inside the federal government. Army Reserve personnel on active duty or performing drills are federal employees/military personnel. Therefore, funding their pay is an internal government matter, not participation with outsiders.
